card.title: The harder practice that worked better

panels.text: In 2006, Rohrer ran a two-part study in which students were taught how to solve maths problems.
Part one compared mass and spaced practice. When tested one week later, the spaced practice group did significantly better.
In part two, practice problems were either grouped by type or mixed randomly. The mixed order felt harder, but those students performed far better.
Why? Students often know the formula but not when to use it. Shuffled problems force you to choose the right method each time.

probes.question: Why might mixed-up practice problems help?
options: They are easier to get through
They make you work out which method fits each problem
They remove the need to know formulas

probes.question: True or false: practising problems grouped by type led to better results than mixing them randomly.
